correctness.rationale: For beta=alpha+2>1, the exact harmonic kernel follows from Fourier-mode weighted norms and reproducing normalization. Scaling and dominated convergence yield p_beta(x)~A_beta|x|^(-beta-1); real and complex beta integrals give the explicit strictly positive A_beta. Cosine integral asymptotics yield fractional and logarithmic dispersion. Fourier-Plancherel yields conditional variance (1+v)^2/(2beta-3), whose beta-prime average gives 2/alpha for alpha>0; tail divergence is sharp otherwise. Direct Fourier transform proves the exact critical E_2 multiplier. All 58 finite diagnostics pass, but do not prove the universal result.

value.rationale: The parameter alpha marks a natural and sharp change in the tangential smoothing scale of a well-studied harmonic Berezin averaging operator: fractional exponent alpha+2, a unit-coefficient logarithmic borderline, and exact ordinary diffusion coefficient 1/alpha. The result determines the kernel tail and all leading constants across the full allowed weight range, providing concrete operator-theoretic frequency benchmarks.
